statement: Four square tiles, each with sides of 1 cm, are put together edge to edge to make one shape. What is the smallest possible distance all the way round the shape?

choices.misconception: I counted the tiles instead of the edges around the outside.
I put the tiles in a row, but that is not the shape with the shortest way round.
I made a big square and took away each shared side once, but a shared side hides two edges.
I added up all the sides of all four tiles, including the sides that touch.

hints: Try a few shapes and count the outside edges of each.
Every time two tiles share a side, two edges are hidden from the outside. The shortest way round comes from the shape where the most sides are shared.
A row of four tiles shares 3 sides. A 2 by 2 square shares 4 sides.

solutions.reliable: The four tiles have 16 edges in all. Each shared side hides 2 edges. A row shares 3 sides, so it measures 16 - 6 = 10 cm round. A 2 by 2 square shares 4 sides, so it measures 16 - 8 = 8 cm round, and no shape of four tiles shares more than 4 sides. The smallest is 8 cm. The idea to keep: the more the tiles touch, the shorter the way round, so a square shape is best.
solutions.elegant: Draw the 2 by 2 square: each side is 2 cm, so the way round is 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 cm. Every other shape of four tiles, like a row or an L, measures 10 cm.

whyOnTest: Same tiles, different shapes, different perimeters: this checks that you compare outside edges, not the number of tiles.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
